extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, practitioners, and U.S. Patent and Trademark Office examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and mandatory requirements for parts, form, and content of U.S. patent applications (models/exhibits, new matter, compact disc submissions, sequence and computer program listings, and arrangement of application elements). Intended to govern how applicants prepare and examiners process application materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention and return of models, exhibits, or specimens
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant is responsible for retaining the actual model, exhibit, or specimen for the enforceable life of any patent resulting from the application except where: (A) the model or exhibit substantially conforms to the requirements of 37 CFR 1.52 or 1.84; (B) the model or exhibit has been described by photographs that substantially conform to 37 CFR 1.84; or (C) the model, exhibit, or specimen is perishable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will notify applicant when the item is no longer necessary and will set a time period (normally one month from mailing, shorter for perishables) within which applicant must arrange return at applicant's expense per 37 CFR 1.94(a). Extensions available under 37 CFR 1.136 except for perishables. Failure to make arrangements within the period will result in disposal under 37 CFR 1.94(c). Applicant may be called upon to resubmit returned items in appropriate circumstances (e.g., continuing application). Form paragraph 6.48 is provided for such notices; Examiner Notes specify perishables policy and special rules for plant specimens (MPEP §1607 and 37 CFR 1.166).

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies of exhibits not ordinarily furnished
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of models or other physical exhibits will not ordinarily be furnished by the Office, and any model or exhibit in an application or patent shall not be taken from the Office except in the custody of an employee of the Office specially authorized by the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should retain originals per retention rules and rely on other permitted representations (photographs, conforming models) where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: No new matter in amendments (37 CFR 1.121)
rubrics_metrics.description: No amendment may introduce new matter into the disclosure of an application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If new matter is introduced into the specification, the amendment should be objected to under 35 U.S.C. 132 (35 U.S.C. 251 for reissue) and the new matter required to be cancelled. If new matter has been entered into or affects claims, the claims should be rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph, because the new matter is not described in the application as originally filed. The examiner must clearly identify the subject matter considered to be new matter. New matter in drawings is ordinarily not entered; substitute sheets containing new matter are likewise ordinarily not entered. An examiner’s holding of new matter may be petitionable or appealable (see MPEP §608.04(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary amendment treatment and obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: A preliminary amendment present on the filing date of the application (filed with the application) is considered part of the original disclosure. A preliminary amendment filed after the filing date is not part of the original disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For applications filed on/after Sept 21, 2004, the Office will automatically treat any preliminary amendment under 37 CFR 1.115(a)(1) present on the filing date as part of the original disclosure. Applicants must ensure preliminary amendments do not contain subject matter not otherwise included in the specification or drawings; if they do, applicant must file a supplemental oath or declaration under 37 CFR 1.67 referring to such preliminary amendment. Failure to submit the required supplemental oath/declaration removes safeguards implied by the oath/declaration requirements. Applicants are strongly encouraged to avoid submitting preliminary amendments to minimize processing burden and delays. During examination, if a preliminary amendment present on the filing date includes unsupported subject matter and the oath/declaration does not refer to it, the examiner may require a supplemental oath/declaration, cancellation of the unsupported subject matter, or a request for reconsideration. For pre-9/21/2004 filings, different rules apply (see MPEP §§714.01(e), 602, 706.03(o)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewability of examiner’s new-matter holding
rubrics_metrics.description: Where alleged new matter is confined to amendments to the specification, review of the examiner’s requirement for cancellation is by way of petition; where the alleged new matter is introduced into or affects the claims (necessitating rejection), the issue is appealable and should not be considered on petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.181 and 1.191 for procedures; practice differs depending on whether claims are involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted documents on compact disc (37 CFR 1.52(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Electronic documents that may be submitted on a compact disc to become permanent USPTO records include: (i) a computer program listing (see §1.96); (ii) a 'Sequence Listing' (see §1.821(c)); or (iii) any individual table if the table is more than 50 pages, or total tables exceed 100 pages (counted per §1.58).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compact discs are defined as CD-ROM or CD-R. CD-RWs are not acceptable. Compact discs filed on the filing date are treated as part of the original disclosure (even if incorporation-by-reference omitted), and the specification must contain an incorporation-by-reference paragraph identifying the disc files (§1.52(e)(5) and §1.77(b)(5)). The Office may require insertion of that statement if omitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compact disc format and labeling requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Each compact disc must conform to ISO 9660 and contents must be in ASCII. CD-R discs must be finalized. Each disc must be enclosed in a hard case within an unsealed padded envelope and accompanied by a paper transmittal letter listing machine format, operating system compatibility, a list of files with names/sizes/dates of creation, and any other special info necessary to identify, maintain, and interpret the data. Compact discs submitted to the Office will not be returned to the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The transmittal letter must also state that the two discs are identical (if two are submitted). The disc must be labeled with inventors' names, title of invention, docket or application number if known, creation date, order if multiple discs (e.g., '1 of X'), and indication 'Copy 1' or 'Copy 2' (see paragraph (e)(6)). If file unreadable on both copies, it will be treated as not submitted (examples: non-compliant format, virus-corrupted, defective disc).

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplicate compact disc submission and replacements
rubrics_metrics.description: Any compact disc must be submitted in duplicate unless it contains only the Sequence Listing in computer readable form required by §1.821(e). The two discs must be labeled 'Copy 1' and 'Copy 2' and the transmittal letter must state they are identical. If not identical, the Office will use 'Copy 1'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments to information on a compact disc must be by replacement compact disc containing the substitute information and accompanied by a statement that the replacement contains no new matter. Replacement discs must be labeled 'COPY 1 REPLACEMENT MM/DD/YYYY' and 'COPY 2 REPLACEMENT MM/DD/YYYY'. A replacement disc must include all unamended files from the original disc plus the amended files (see form paragraph 6.72.05).

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling unreadable or infected compact discs
rubrics_metrics.description: If a file is unreadable on both copies of the disc, the unreadable file will be treated as not having been submitted. If a compact disc contains viruses, it is objected to and correction is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of unreadable: wrong format (not ISO 9660/ASCII), corrupted by a virus, written onto a defective disc. OPAP will check discs for viruses, readability, non-ASCII files, and labeling compliance and will notify applicant for corrections. Provisional applications get special notifications and correction requirements when discs are infected or unreadable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper-size equivalence and application-size fee treatment for electronic listings
rubrics_metrics.description: Any sequence listing or computer program listing in electronic medium in compliance with §§1.52(e) and 1.821(c)/(e) and §1.96 will be excluded when determining the application size fee under §1.16(s) or §1.492(j). For other electronic submissions, each three kilobytes of content submitted on an electronic medium is counted as a sheet of paper for fee purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For Office electronic filing system submissions, paper size equivalent is determined after rendering by the system; sequence and program listings submitted in ASCII as part of an associated file submitted via EFS may be excluded per paragraph (f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrangement and required sections of the specification (37 CFR 1.77)
rubrics_metrics.description: The elements of the application should appear in a specified order (utility application transmittal form; fee transmittal; application data sheet; specification; drawings; executed oath/declaration). The specification should include sections in order: title of the invention; cross-reference to related applications; statement of federally sponsored research; names of parties to joint research agreement; reference to Sequence Listing/table/computer program listing on compact disc and incorporation-by-reference; background; brief summary; brief description of drawing views; detailed description; claim(s); abstract; Sequence Listing if on paper (37 CFR 1.77(b)(1)-(12)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text of these sections should be preceded by uppercase section headings without underlining or bold type. The specification must identify compact disc(s) and list files and total number of discs (see §1.52(e)(5)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compact disc storage, handling, and replacement procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Compact discs should be enclosed in a hard case, kept in the compact disc holder provided in each application file, and not scratched or exposed to heat/humidity. OPAP will retain one copy and place the other in the application file jacket; if a disc is damaged or lost, OPAP will make a duplicate replacement from its retained copy and provide replacement at allowance if required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replacement disc requests should be forwarded to OPAP. Examiners may view files using text readers or MS Word on their workstations; special text viewing software is provided in Technology Centers as needed. Replacement compact discs for amendments must include all current files to ensure a single latest set is available for Office, printer, and public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraphs for compact disc deficiencies (use and examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: A set of form paragraphs (e.g., ¶6.60.01, ¶6.61.01, ¶6.61.02, ¶6.62, ¶6.70.01, ¶6.71.01, ¶6.71.02, ¶6.72.01–6.72.05) are provided to notify applicants of specific CD issues: missing statement that CDs are identical; missing list of compact discs and/or associated files in the specification; missing incorporation-by-reference statement for the compact disc; data file not in ASCII; transmittal letter omissions; CDs not identical; CDs not readable; CDs contain viruses; missing files on replacement discs; etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each form paragraph includes required corrective action and Examiner Notes specifying bracket insertions and when to use the paragraph. Examples: ¶6.62 must be used when submitted data file is not ASCII; ¶6.72.05 when replacement disc fails to include all unamended files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computer program listing submission rules (37 CFR 1.96)
rubrics_metrics.description: Descriptions of operation and general content of computer program listings should appear in the description portion of the specification. A computer program listing is a printout listing instructions, routines, and contents of a program; it may be in machine or machine-independent (object or source) language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the listing is ≤300 lines (each line ≤72 characters) it may be submitted as drawings or as part of the specification. If submitted as drawings, must comply with §1.84 and have at least one figure numeral on each sheet. If submitted in the specification and having more than 60 lines, it must be positioned at the end of the description but before the claims; any amendment must be by substitute sheet. Any listing >300 lines (up to 72 chars/line) must be submitted on compact disc as a 'computer program listing appendix' (will not be printed) and the specification must reference it at the location indicated in §1.77(b)(5). Multiple listings may be on one disc; separate compact disc is required for each application containing such an appendix. The appendix disc must meet strict specifications (computer compatibility: IBM PC/XT/AT or compatibles or Apple Macintosh; OS compatibility: MS-DOS, MS-Windows, Unix, or Macintosh; line terminator: ASCII CR+LF; control codes: only ASCII-defined characters; compression: uncompressed). No other formats allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation and amendment rules for sequence listings and large tables
rubrics_metrics.description: Sequence listings and large tables have specific submission criteria: sequence listings may be submitted on compact disc in compliance with §1.821(c)/(e); an individual table >50 pages or total tables >100 pages may be submitted on compact disc as allowed under §1.52(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The specification must include an incorporation-by-reference paragraph identifying each disc and the files, their dates and sizes in bytes. Any amendment to material on a compact disc must be by way of a replacement compact disc in compliance with §1.52(e) containing the substitute information and accompanied by a statement that the replacement contains no new matter. No new matter may be introduced when presenting files in ASCII or ISO 9660 format (form paragraphs emphasize 'No new matter may be introduced').
